findings: The primary specimen is a convincing Northern Rough-winged Swallow: plain brown upperparts, dingy gray-brown throat and chest grading into a whitish belly, small rounded head, short dark bill, dark eye, long pointed wings, short shallow-notched tail, and short dark legs and feet agree with the reference photographs and direct-source descriptions.

The plate contains exactly one complete primary specimen with one head, one beak, two anatomically coherent folded wings, two attached legs with intact gripping feet, and one tail. The far-side structures are naturally overlapped rather than missing or duplicated.

The detached wing and bill/head studies are clearly supplementary. The wing study has coherent feather layering and a broad-based pointed profile; the head study has a complete, proportionate bill consistent with the primary specimen and side-profile references.
The common name, scientific name, and family are correctly spelled and independently verified as Northern Rough-winged Swallow, Stelgidopteryx serripennis, and Hirundinidae.

All three printed measurements exactly match the proposed profile and Cornell's published ranges: length 12–15 cm (4.7–5.9 in), wingspan 27–30 cm (10.6–11.8 in), and weight 10–18 g (0.3–0.6 oz). Audubon independently agrees on the length and wingspan ranges and gives a narrower weight range within the plate's published range.
The habitat paragraph, behavior paragraph, and all six field-mark bullets are complete, grammatical, and match the proposed wording without omissions, substitutions, duplication, or nonsensical text.

The vertical body-length diagram is internally consistent: 12 cm (4.7 in) is the lower endpoint, 15 cm (5.9 in) is the upper endpoint, values increase from bottom to top, the adjacent range matches the printed measurement, and the explicit “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE” label prevents it from representing the printed bird's physical size.
The wing-pattern and bill/head captions are correct, and the four palette labels—WARM BROWN, GRAY-BROWN, DIRTY WHITE, and CHARCOAL BLACK—are legible and consistent with the depicted plumage.
The layout is balanced, readable, and scientifically useful; the primary specimen remains dominant while the supplementary studies, scale, and palette are clearly separated.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears anywhere on the plate.
